headline: Volvo and Waabi have started hauling freight with self-driving trucks between Dallas and Houston for logistics firm Warp, with an observer still in the driver's seat.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a first customer lane on a major Texas freight route for two autonomous-truck makers, though with a human observer on board and only company statements behind it.
importance_line: Warp and the shippers and carriers using its network on the Dallas-Houston route are the first customers to rely on these trucks, but an observer still sits in the driver's seat, no date is given for driverless runs and the performance claims are the companies' own.
summary: Robotics & Automation News reports, quoting company executives, that Volvo Autonomous Solutions and the self-driving developer Waabi have begun carrying freight on Volvo VNL Autonomous trucks, powered by Waabi's self-driving technology (the Waabi Driver), along the Dallas-Houston route for logistics software company Warp, their first customer operation together. Waabi's chief operating officer says it shows the trucks can handle the full range of freight, including less-than-truckload networks that combine goods from several customers on tightly coordinated schedules, and the two firms say they will use the lane to prepare more routes.
notes: Read in full. The text reads like the companies' joint announcement (all quotes from Volvo, Waabi and Warp executives), so CONFIRMED for the launch itself; nothing independently checked, so performance claims are attributed to the companies. The article says autonomous hauls currently run with an observer in the driver's seat; that hedge is in the headline and importance line.
